September, 2024

Author: S.K. Sahoo
Bench: S.K. Sahoo
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Crla No. 391 of 2024
 Jagamohan Swain .... Appellant
 Mr. D. K. Das, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha & another .... Respondents

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Standing Counsel
 Coram:
 The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.K. Sahoo
 Order
Order No. 13.09.2024
05.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Video Conferencing/Physical Mode).
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State.
None appears for the informant respondent no.2 in spite of service of notice.

This is an appeal under section 14-A of S.C. & S.T. Act in connection with Special G.R. Case No.41 of 2023 arising out of Gop P.S. Case No.275 of 2023 pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Nimapara for offences punishable under sections 341/376(2)(n)/506 of the Indian Penal Code, sections 3(1)(r)(s)(W-i)/2(v)(va) of the S.C. & S.T.
(PoA) Act and section 67 of the I.T. Act.

entities.text: Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Nimapara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant moved an application for bail before the Court of Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Nimapara, which was rejected on 08.04.2024.

entities.text: Court of Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Nimapara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is in judicial custody since 14.06.2023.

Earlier the appellant approached this Court for bail in CRLA No.796 of 2023 and as per order dated 07.11.2023, the prayer for bail was rejected, however liberty was granted to the Jagamohan Swain vs State Of Odisha & Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162545449/
1 appellant to renew the prayer for bail after examination of the victim in the trial Court.

entities.text: Jagamohan Swain vs State Of Odisha & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submitted that in the meantime, the victim has been examined in the trial Court as P.W.1 and though she has supported the prosecution, but it appears that she is a consenting party.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and on verification of the records, he submitted that there is no criminal antecedent against the appellant.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the nature of evidence adduced by the victim, the period of detention of the appellant in judicial custody and absence of any criminal antecedent against the appellant, I am inclined to re- consider the prayer for bail and direct the appellant to be released on bail.

Let the appellant be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper with further conditions that he shall not indulge in any criminal activities, shall appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case would be posted for trial and shall not come in contact with the victim or any other witnesses yet to be examined in the trial Court.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
